articles.title: Nations Championship: Fixtures, schedule, dates, key info about rugby's revolutionary new-look tournament
articles.summary: World Rugby’s 12-team Nations Championship launches in 2026, uniting Six Nations sides with Rugby Championship teams plus Fiji and Japan; Tournament splits six fixtures across northern and southern hemisphere from July before Finals Weekend at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham in November
articles.body:
The Nations Championship is World Rugby's new 12-team tournament that pits the giants of northern and southern hemisphere rugby against each other on a more consistent basis.

The tournament is designed to align northern and southern hemisphere rugby calendars, guaranteeing high-profile fixtures to add more structure and meaning to the existing international windows between World Cups.

The Six Nations teams - England, France, Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Italy - will take on the four Rugby Championship sides - South Africa, New Zealand, Australia, Argentina (SANZAAR) - with Fiji and Japan also representing the south hemisphere.

The inaugural Nations Championship begins in July 2026.

Subsequent tournaments will be held biennially, in every year that does not feature a men's Rugby World Cup or a British and Irish Lions tour.

Each team will play six matches: three in July in the southern hemisphere and three in November in the northern hemisphere.

Twickenham's Allianz Stadium will then host Finals Weekend from November 27 to 29, where the inaugural champions will be crowned.

Rankings for Finals Weekend will be determined by results from the opening six matches, with each northern hemisphere team playing an additional fixture against the correspondingly ranked southern side.

England will launch their first Nations Championship campaign in South Africa, before facing Fiji and Argentina.

Ireland face Australia, Japan and New Zealand, who host France and Italy in their first two games.

Scotland play Argentina, South Africa and Fiji, with Wales taking on the Springboks after facing Fiji and Argentina.

Six Nations chief executive Tom Harrison believes the Nations Championship will transform rugby, unlocking its value for the benefit of the sport and its fans.

"The Nations Championship has the power to redefine the future of rugby, and the partnership between Six Nations Rugby and SANZAAR signals a tectonic shift in the sport," he said.

"Rugby's strongest nations have collaborated with a clear vision to grow the game, by challenging traditional ways of operating to create a tournament structure with genuine global relevance, which will unlock the true value of the sport.

"The world's biggest and best championships are defined by intense sporting drama, and the Nations Championship will stand alongside these.

"The Finals Weekend will add a totally new dimension for fans, and promises to create an incredible spectacle, crown champions, and act as a catalyst to grow rugby's reach, globally.

"By bringing together the best teams and players in the sport and injecting another layer to the fierce cross-hemisphere rivalries, the Nations Championship will take international rugby to new heights."

You need look no further than Argentina's meteoric rise since joining the Rugby Championship in 2012 to appreciate the scale of opportunity now facing Fiji and Japan.

Fiji have consistently punched above their weight on the world stage, and with regular Test matches against Tier 1 opposition built into the calendar, their potential has no ceiling.

Japan's momentum, which surged during the last decade, may have slowed since hosting the 2019 Rugby World Cup yet their Nations Championship berth offers fresh impetus, reaffirming their status and potential as a true rugby nation.

'Slap in the face' - closed shop criticism

The overhaul of the summer and autumn international windows has raised concerns about the real-world threat the Nations Championship poses to emerging rugby nations.

Georgia - who are 11th in the World Rankings, above Wales and Japan - have contentiously been overlooked.

World Rugby has guaranteed regular Test matches against Tier 1 opposition to the likes of Georgia, Samoa, Tonga and Uruguay, but the opportunity for Tier 2 nations to develop against the world's best will significantly diminish.

With the sporadic scheduling of fixtures, often against each other, those excluded face the prospect of the gap between themselves and the established Tier 1 nations widening.

Promotion or relegation will also not come into force in the Nations Championship until at least 2030, further strengthening the Tier 2 nations' claims the tournament is a closed shop.

Former All Blacks and current Samoa international Lima Sopoaga labelled the Nations Championship a "slap in the face" that "undermines the spirit of inclusivity that rugby is supposed to stand for."

July 11 New Zealand vs Italy Japan vs Ireland South Africa vs Scotland Australia vs France Fiji vs England Argentina vs Wales

July 18 Japan vs France Australia vs Italy South Africa vs Wales New Zealand vs Ireland Fiji vs Scotland Argentina vs England

November 6-8 Ireland vs Argentina Scotland vs New Zealand France vs Fiji Italy vs South Africa Wales vs Japan England vs Australia

November 13-15 France vs South Africa Wales vs New Zealand Ireland vs Fiji Italy vs Argentina England vs Japan Scotland vs Australia

articles.title: Scott Hastings: Scottish rugby great and former British and Irish Lions centre dies aged 61
articles.summary: Scott Hastings has died aged 61; the Scottish rugby great was diagnosed with cancer in 2022; Hastings, who featured for the British and Irish Lions at centre, won 65 Test caps in an 11-year international career
articles.body:
The British and Irish Lions centre won 65 caps in an 11-year Test career that began in 1986 and was part of the most recent Scotland team to win the Grand Slam in 1990.

A statement released by his son Corey and daughter Kerry-Anne revealed he died due to complications arising from cancer treatment.

Hastings, younger brother of fellow Scotland international and British & Irish Lion Gavin, announced in 2022 he had been diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma.

"We are saddened to inform you that Scott passed away peacefully surrounded by family on the morning of Sunday, May 17," the statement read.

"This also marked his late wife Jenny's birthday which speaks louder than words that he is safe and with his beloved Jenny.

"Scott was undergoing cancer treatment and due to complications deteriorated extremely quickly. Despite every effort by the incredible team at the Western General ICU, he passed away peacefully and pain free.

"At this time, the family ask everyone to give them space to process and manage their energies and ask for their privacy to be respected.

"More information will be shared in due course to celebrate Scott's incredible life."

articles.title: Women's Six Nations: How England's Red Roses defied the odds to create more history with Grand Slam triumph in Bordeaux
articles.summary: England’s Red Roses navigated pregnancies, injuries and setbacks to claim an historic fifth straight Grand Slam, extending their unbeaten run to 38 Tests and reaffirming their status as the dominant force in women’s rugby
articles.body:
The Red Roses had to navigate it all during the 2026 Six Nations, and yet one thing endured: their status as the elite of women's rugby.

Hot on the heels of last year's World Cup triumph, Sunday's 43-28 victory over France in Bordeaux saw the Red Roses clinch an historic fifth successive Grand Slam.

It saw England's all-conquering women's rugby stars secure an eighth consecutive Women's Six Nations title while extending their winning run to 38 Tests.

Red Roses make more history against the odds

Despite entering the tournament as world champions, a period of unsettling change in the Red Roses camp gave renewed optimism to those hoping to dethrone them.

World Cup‑winning captain Zoe Stratford, locks Abbie Ward and Rosie Galligan, and hooker Lark Atkin‑Davies all missed the campaign due to pregnancy, while forwards Hannah Botterman and May Campbell, along with back Tatyana Heard, were ruled out through injury.

Once the tournament began, England faced further setbacks, with Alex Matthews, Natasha Hunt, and Morwenna Talling sustaining tournament‑ending injuries after round one.

The 2026 Six Nations became the most thorough examination yet of England's strength in depth - but with five debutants blooded across the campaign, they once again proved they had the answers.

They showed the wherewithal, tenacity, and determination to overcome the absence of a host of World Cup winners and secure yet more history.

'Hardest Six Nations' declares emotional Mitchell

Reflecting on the scale of the Red Roses' achievement against all odds, John Mitchell couldn't hide his emotion.

He said: "It was great to win a World Cup at home, but what we've navigated in this tournament - the youth and energy coming through, while our mates are at home becoming mums or going through rehab - these girls are just so brave, unbelievable, and driven. They are courageous all the time.

"This has been the hardest Six Nations, which is why I've been so emotional. I've got to take my hat off to the players and the coaching staff. They have been awesome in navigating so much change."

For many, this latest success puts this Red Roses cohort firmly in the bracket of the best ever to do it in an England shirt.

Victory in Bordeaux brought an eighth successive Six Nations title, something never previously achieved by any side - England or otherwise.

Between 2006 and 2012 England won seven straight Six Nations titles but this side has now gone one better, winning every championship since 2019.

Clinching a Grand Slam at The Stade Atlantique also created history - a fifth clean sweep in a row, which has never been done. In fact, no team bar this side has achieved four in a row, and in the men's game, no side has ever won back-to-back Slams.

This Red Roses side also became the first rugby outfit in the women's or men's game to win a Six Nations the year after clinching a Rugby World Cup triumph, eclipsing the achievements of the Red Roses vintage of 2014 and Clive Woodward's 2003 England men's World Cup champions. There was no women's championship in 1995 after the Red Roses' 1994 World Cup win.

With an unbeaten Test run since 2022 and now 38 Test victories in a row, there could even be an argument that this is the greatest sports side in history. Has anyone dominated like this Red Roses class have?

The question before the Six Nations began was whether anyone could stop the Red Roses.

Five formidable victories and another Grand Slam later, it's back to the drawing board for their European rivals to devise another plan to bring an end to their dynasty.

France ran them as close as any team has in the competition, but there was still a sizeable gulf in class - and in how deep that class runs.

What's more, Sunday's clash played out in a year that really felt like France's best chance since they last beat England in 2018.

Les Bleues had home advantage for the decider, in front of a raucous full house, had matched England for bonus-point wins leading up to it, and England were missing a host of players.

Remarkably, England clinched this crown on French soil while missing eight of the 13 forwards from last year's World Cup final squad.

For full-back Ellie Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - this England side still have room to grow too.

"We've won a Grand Slam but there is still so much room to grow. That is exciting," she said to the BBC following victory.

"It's hard to sum up the emotions. It's never been done before [five Grand Slams]. To be part of a team that makes history again is something I'm very proud of.

"We knew it wouldn't be easy today, we knew what was coming, but I'm so proud of the girls. Grand Slam baby!

"We've had to show how adaptable we are as a team. I don't think there has ever been a time where so many people have been mixing and matching, but it shows the depth in English rugby and the culture of our team to bring new people in."

articles.title: England Rugby: Benhard Janse van Rensburg, Charlie Bracken, Archie McParland called up as George Martin returns in Nations Championship training squad
articles.summary: Benhard Janse van Rensburg and Charlie Bracken, son of former England scrum-half Kyran, are among those called up to Steve Borthwick's England squad for three-day training camp ahead of the inaugural Nations Championship
articles.body:
Bristol centre Van Rensburg will complete his five-year eligibility period on July 8 - notably, four days after England's opening match against South Africa - and is seen as a potentially key midfield option in the run up to the 2027 World Cup.

The Pretoria-born centre, who joined London Irish in 2021, will qualify through residency after the RFU successfully lobbied World Rugby to bring his eligibility date forward from November. He had previously made one substitute appearance for South Africa under-20s in 2016.

Bracken, son of former England scrum-half Kyran, has also been given his first call-up by Steve Borthwick and will join up with team-mates at the Performance Centre at Pennyhill Park until Wednesday.

McParland made his Saints debut as a 17-year-old against London Irish in September 2022.

The squad also features an international return for highly-rated lock George Martin, who gets a call-up for the first time since February 2025 having suffered a combination of knee and shoulder injuries that had kept him out of action for 14 months.

Winger Noah Caluori, who was previously selected in the squad for last autumn's internationals, has scored tries for fun in all competitions this season for Saracens as well also playing in the Championship under dual registration for Ampthill.

Notable absentees from Borthwick's selection include Bath pair Ollie Lawrence and Henry Arundell. The centre and winger have both been omitted on form rather than fitness.

Van Rensburg will be eligible after England's opening Nations Championship fixture against his native country in Johannesburg on Saturday July 4 and could make his debut against Fiji at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday July 11.

Van Rensburg inclusion key to England's puzzle

Van Rensburg's inclusion in this England training squad is a really interesting and exciting selection.

"He's six foot tall, he's 17 stone, he's a very imposing physical ball carrier, he's also got a really good offloading game too and defensively solid.

"We thought he would be available, become available, for Steve Borthwick in the autumn, but actually he's going to be available sooner, this summer.

"He won't be available for the South Africa game which is in Johannesburg on July the 4th but he will be for the games that follow it against Fiji and Argentina and the fact he's in this squad suggests Borthwick has every intention of blooding him.

"He has that typically South African attribute of immense physicality and for that reason is a really exciting prospect.

"There are a few surprise or notable omissions in this squad too. Ollie Lawrence, a man who's been the mainstay in England's midfield for a number of years now, is not included.

"That is a surprise because he's not injured, he's not been included on form and neither has his Bath teammate Henry Arundel despite scoring nine tries in his last seven games."

England training squad ahead of Nations Championship

Jamie Blamire (Leicester Tigers), Ollie Chessum (Leicester Tigers), Arthur Clark (Gloucester Rugby), Alex Coles (Northampton Saints), Chandler Cunningham-South (Harlequins), Tom Curry (Sale Sharks), Theo Dan (Saracens), Alex Dombrandt (Harlequins), Ben Earl (Saracens), Ellis Genge (Bristol Bears), Jamie George (Saracens), Joe Heyes (Leicester Tigers), Nick Isiekwe (Saracens), Maro Itoje (Saracens), Emmanuel Iyogun (Northampton Saints), George Martin (Leicester Tigers), Beno Obano (Bath Rugby), Asher Opoku-Fordjour (Sale Sharks), Guy Pepper (Bath Rugby), Henry Pollock (Northampton Saints), Vilikesa Sela (Bath Rugby), Kepu Tuipulotu (Bath Rugby).

Seb Atkinson (Gloucester Rugby), Charlie Bracken (Saracens), Noah Caluori (Saracens), Fraser Dingwall (Northampton Saints), Immanuel Feyi-Waboso (Exeter Chiefs), George Ford (Sale Sharks), Tommy Freeman (Northampton Saints), George Furbank (Northampton Saints), Benhard Janse van Rensburg (Bristol Bears), Archie McParland (Northampton Saints), Alex Mitchell (Northampton Saints), Cadan Murley (Harlequins), Adam Radwan (Leicester Tigers), Tom Roebuck (Sale Sharks), Henry Slade (Exeter Chiefs), Fin Smith (Northampton Saints), Marcus Smith (Harlequins), Ben Spencer (Bath Rugby), Freddie Steward (Leicester Tigers), Jack van Poortvliet (Leicester Tigers).

Not considered for selection: Fin Baxter (Harlequins), Ben Curry (Sale Sharks), Elliot Daly (Saracens), Trevor Davison (Northampton Saints), Greg Fisilau (Exeter Chiefs), Will Muir (Bath Rugby), Bevan Rodd (Sale Sharks), Sam Underhill (Bath Rugby).

articles.title: Gallagher Prem: Tom Wills crowned Prem player of the season ahead of Bordeaux switch
articles.summary: Tom Willis of Saracens wins Gallagher Prem player of the season; the No 8 has signed for Bordeaux for the 2026/27 season onwards, meaning he will be unavailable for international selection in a blow to Steve Borthwick's England
articles.body:
Willis came out top in a vote by players across the league after a seismic campaign at StoneX Stadium that saw him lead the stats for most carries, defenders beaten and off-loads.

The 27-year-old's ability to break tackles, combined with his physicality in defence, helped take Saracens to the brink of the play-offs, only to be denied by Exeter on the final day of the regular season last Saturday.

In a blow to England, the 6ft 4in, 19-stone back row told Steve Borthwick in October that he had signed for a second spell at Bordeaux, making him unavailable for international selection from next season.

Borthwick chose to overlook him for the autumn and Six Nations in favour of investing in players who would be available for the 2027 World Cup, even though Willis had already been given an enhanced England EPS contract worth in the region of £160,000.

It means one of the nation's most destructive forwards has been able to add to his eight caps in 2025-26 yet he now returns to the Top 14 with the acclaim of his fellow professionals.

In a double for Saracens, 19-year-old wing sensation Noah Caluori was named breakthrough player of season and also finished as top try scorer with 18 touch downs.

Northampton's Phil Dowson took the director of rugby prize for guiding Saints to a first-place finish at the end of the regular season, despite operating on the third lowest salary cap spend in the competition.

articles.title: Nations Championship: England call up Tom Roebuck for Fiji and Argentina games after George Furbank surgery
articles.summary: Tom Roebuck joins England squad for Fiji (July 11) and Argentina (July 18) Tests in Nations Championship after George Furbank ruled out following appendix surgery; England lost Nations Championship opener 45-21 to South Africa in Johannesburg on Saturday
articles.body:
Furbank underwent surgery in South Africa to have his appendix removed on the eve of England's 45-21 defeat to the Springboks in Johannesburg.

It was the latest setback for Northampton's Furbank, who has battled a succession of injuries since his last England outing in November 2024 to earn a place back in Steve Borthwick's squad.

Marcus Smith replaced Furbank in England's starting XV at Ellis Park, but Sale back Roebuck has been drafted in to provide additional cover.

England are hosted by Fiji at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on Saturday before the squad travels to Argentina to face Los Pumas on July 18.

Borthwick backs players after late yellow cards

Meanwhile, Borthwick defended Tommy Freeman and Guy Pepper, who were both shown yellow cards late on in Saturday's defeat.

Freeman was sent to the sin bin for a dangerous tackle in the 71st minute and a minute later Pepper followed him into the stands for a late challenge.

That meant the tourists were forced to play the final seven minutes of their Nations Championship opener with only 13 men and they leaked tries to Malcolm Marx and BJ Dixon in the closing minutes to complete a harrowing evening in Johannesburg.

However, Borthwick refused to blame either player.

He said: "If you look at the Tommy Freeman one you see a slight timing error, there wasn't anything malicious or reckless there. He was trying to make a tackle and he was apologetic for the tackling height.

"The Guy Pepper one, South Africa put players under pressure because that is the way they play and they are very good.

"We want our execution and decision-making to be at a very high level and these young players will learn from this experience of playing against the best in the world."

England have now been hit with 10 yellow cards and one red in their six games in 2026.

The theme of ill-discipline was raised by their post-Six Nations review as an area of concern and Jamie George, who is captaining the side in place of the rested Maro Itoje, admitted that part of their game needs to be better.

He said: "There are some clear things we need to make sure we get better at and as players we have to take a lot more responsibility with regards to our discipline, which let us down.

"Outside of that, there were periods where we put the Springboks under a lot of pressure. Speaking to their guys they know they have been in a Test match.

"We are going to be a significantly better team off the back of this experience with a young team coming here and understanding how we put them under a lot of pressure and also understanding how we let that pressure get to us a little bit.

"This is going to be a great learning experience for us, but we are gutted because we genuinely believed we could come here and win.

"We are going to rally round, stay tight and we are all looking forward to getting to Liverpool and putting in a great performance against Fiji."

Fin Smith also offered an honest appraisal of England's defeat, alleging Borthwick's side were "soft" in defence at Ellis Park.

"We still have to question why we started as poorly as we did," Smith said. "For about 50 minutes of that game you saw how we wanted to play but then, ultimately, they were too good for us in the end.

"I'm actually more frustrated about how we started rather than how it went at the end. At the end, down to 13, we were still fighting against a top side like that.

"It is understandable, 15 against 13, they might get a few but for us to start as poorly as we did was more frustrating.

"We were soft defensively, missed a lot of tackles and ultimately they scored quickly when they got into our 22.

"Deep down I'm probably pretty proud of our efforts, we stuck in it, but we gave ourselves too much to do."

vs Fiji (July 11) - Hill Dickinson Stadium, Liverpool (2.10pm)

vs Argentina (July 18) - Estadio Unico, Santiago del Estero (8.10pm)

articles.title: Nations Championship - Fiji 8-73 England: Henry Pollock scores hat-trick as Steve Borthwick's side end five-Test losing run after Fiji red card
articles.summary: Henry Pollock scores second-half hat-trick as England demolish Fiji after Simione Kuruvoli red card in first half for kicking out at Ellis Genge; Marcus Smith, Jamie George, Guy Pepper, Benhard Janse van Rensburg, Gus Atkinson, Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Henry Slade, Noah Caluori also score
articles.body:
A dominant first-half display saw Marcus Smith and Jamie George score early tries - the opener after a bizarre corner flag assist - before Guy Pepper, Benhard Janse van Rensburg and Gus Atkinson added further efforts with Levani Botia in the sin-bin for cynical play.

Janse van Rensburg - a controversial import from South Africa for whom England had to get World Rugby approval to select - scored with his first touch on debut, having come on while Henry Slade was undergoing a HIA.

Fiji appeared to have ended the half with a try through Kalaveti Ravouvou in the final play, but it was ruled out with scrum-half Simione Kuruvoli shown a harsh permanent red card for kicking out at Ellis Genge - referee Hollie Davidson and TMO Mike Adamson refusing to sanction Genge for holding onto the legs of Kuruvoli prior to the act.

Such an officiating decision rendered the second 40 minutes a virtual non-contest with Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Henry Pollock (hat-trick), Slade and debutant Noah Caluori each scoring after Tevita Ikanivere had crossed for Fiji's only try.

In terms of why a Fiji 'home' game against England during a touring summer was played in Liverpool, the decision lay with Fiji's rugby union before the start of the Nations Championship - the feeling being they could make more money by staging their July contests in Europe.

Yet, Fiji struggled for possession and were second best to England's scrum, maul and defence in a first half which saw Fiji concede nine penalties, lose Botia to the sin-bin and, eventually, Kuruvoli for the remainder.

Smith's try in the sixth minute brought with it a hefty bit of fortune to get England going - Fin Smith sending over a cross-field kick which evaded the chasing Tommy Freeman, but struck the corner flag to run back infield for Marcus Smith to ground.

Following a long-range Caleb Muntz penalty, England had their second try through George via a dominant rolling maul drive, and were soon facing 14 players when Botia was shown yellow for diving over a ruck near his own tryline.

Pepper battled his way over nearly immediately, with former South Africa U20 centre Janse van Rensburg then diving over just 218 seconds after coming on as an HIA replacement for Slade and three days after qualifying for England on residency grounds.

Atkinson scored England's fifth when collecting a Jack van Poortvliet offload before the break, with Kuruvoli then dismissed and Genge fortunate to avoid a sin-binning for provoking the kick out.

The onslaught intensified in the second half even though Borthwick emptied his bench, with 19-year-old rookie Caluori touching down in the 65th minute and the rapid Pollock, another replacement, completing his hat-trick in the closing seconds.

The victory was England's biggest since beating Chile 71-0 in Lille at the 2023 Rugby World Cup.

Relieved of the burden of their losing run, England head to Argentina for the climax to their July tour with renewed purpose but the Pumas at Santiago del Estero will prove a far sterner test.

Borthwick: Mitchell ruled out of Argentina Test with hamstring injury

Alex Mitchell has been ruled out of England's final Nations Championship match against Argentina after sustaining a hamstring injury.

Mitchell came on as a second-half replacement for Jack van Poortvliet but lasted just nine minutes before limping off and cut a frustrated figure as he left the field.

The British and Irish Lions scrum-half's season has been hampered by two previous hamstring injuries, the first of which ruled him out of the Six Nations, and he will now miss the climax to the July tour in Santiago del Estero.

Head coach Steve Borthwick said: "I don't know at this stage whether it's a recurrence of the hamstring injury he's had a couple of times already this season, nor can I confirm the length at this early stage of how long he's going to be absent for, but it looks like he won't be able to be part of next week."

'A clinic from England on how to beat dangerous opposition'

Former England international Danny Care speaking to ITV :

"England have put on a clinic today on how to win a Test match against a really dangerous opposition.

"They bounced back. They've improved in every aspect of the game that they did last week in South Africa.

"They were clinical, they played in the right areas and when they had opportunities to score, they did.

"And they had a bit of razzle dazzle at the end with Henry Pollock scoring his hat-trick.

"A great day for England and back to where they should be, back to winning ways.

"Next week becomes massive away in Argentina. That'll be a whole different level than what today was."

England travel to face Argentina for their third Nations Championship fixture as they face the Pumas at Estadio Unico in Santiago del Estero on Saturday July 18 (8.10pm kick-off).

Fiji next face Scotland for their third Test of the summer, also on Saturday July 18, at Murrayfield in Edinburgh (2.10pm kick-off).

articles.title: Nations Championship: Much-changed Ireland overcome Japan 36-20 as debutants impress
articles.summary: Nick Timoney, Tom O'Toole and Robbie Henshaw scored in the first half before Sean Jansen and Tom Stewart added scores in the second half as Ireland beat Japan in Australia; Ireland have now picked up victories in their opening two games in the Nations Championship
articles.body:
Andy Farrell's side followed up their thrilling comeback victory over Australia last week with a solid performance at McDonald Jones Stadium in Newcastle, Australia on Saturday morning – with debutant Sean Jansen scoring and picking up the player of the match award in an impressive performance as Ireland picked up the bonus point victory to remain top of the Northern Hemisphere group.

The victory secured a full haul of 10 points from their opening two games in the new global competition, and coach Andy Farrell was able to hand debuts ‌to four players.

All in, the Ireland head coach made nine changes and blooded more new talent as rookie Connacht props Billy Bohan and Sam Illo, as well as Ulster back row Bryn Ward, also made their debuts after coming off the bench – but it was Jansen who claimed the headlines with his display.

"I'm so privileged to wear this jersey," said Jansen to Virgin Media Sport after the game. "What a win! When we found out, when the team got selected, us boys were so stoked, it was a dream come true."

Tadhg Beirne captained Ireland for the first time and hooker Ronan Kelleher picked up his 50th cap but Japan, technically the home side for the fixture, took an early lead with a 60-metre try from wing Taira Main as he broke the Irish defensive line.

That only served to rouse the Irish forwards, who got to ‌work and had too much power for their opponents, with flanker Nick Timoney and prop Tom O'Toole crossing for tries before centre Robbie Henshaw added a third ‌before halftime to ensure Ireland led by six points at the break – but Takuro Matsunaga scored two penalties to keep Japan in touch.

Number eight Jansen, who showcased his dynamism and discipline with a dozen carries and 14 tackles, crashed over on his Ireland debut 10 minutes into the second half as the forwards carried on making metres before replacement hooker Hayate Era responded for Japan eight minutes later to keep the Cherry Blossoms within a converted try of the lead heading into the final quarter of the game.

Harry Byrne's penalty nine minutes from time provided daylight for Ireland and they managed to hold on and Era was sent to the sin bin after multiple infringements in the 77th minute.

Tom Stewart completed the scoring by latching onto a pass from Nathan Doak and crossing to cap off a fine victory for Ireland with Byrne adding the extras just as Ciaran Frawley had done three times earlier in the game.

Japan will take plenty from the game following their victory over Italy last weekend, and only trailed by six points with 10 minutes remaining. It was another impressive performance against the side ranked third in the world, reflecting their recent progression under coach Eddie Jones.

Next up for Ireland, is a trip to face the All Blacks in Auckland, but Farrell's squad will benefit from the respite afforded to key players such as tour captain Dan Sheehan, Tadhg Furlong, Jamison Gibson-Park, Sam Prendergast, Garry Ringrose and Hugo Keenan ahead of next weekend's clash.

articles.title: Nations Championship - Argentina 35-21 Wales: Los Pumas bounce back as Wales fail to build on strong start
articles.summary: Argentina responded to their home loss against Scotland last weekend by comfortably defeating Wales in the Nations Championship; visitors outscored by five tries to three; Wales travel to South Africa to face world champions next Saturday
articles.body:
An early try from Dewi Lake gave Steve Tandy's side an early lead but the Pumas quickly responded with the first two of their five tries.

Rhys Carre pulled Wales back level but three more tries in a 13-minute spell either side of half-time gave the hosts a commanding lead before Ben Warren's consolation.

Sam Costelow converted all three of Wales' tries but Argentina, for whom Joaquin Oviedo starred with two touchdowns, deserved their victory as they bounced back impressively from defeat to Scotland.

They controlled the game for long periods with further scores for Justo Piccardo, Marcos Kremer and Santiago Carreras while 10 points came via the boot of Tomas Albornoz.

Wales, buoyed by last week's win over Fiji, made a superb start as Lake drove over in the fourth minute but his effort was quickly cancelled out as Oviedo finished off an Argentina break two minutes later.

The Pumas took the lead for the first time through Piccardo but his effort owed much to the brilliance of Bautista Delguy, who caught a high ball and offloaded in one motion.

Wales thought they had replied when Jac Morgan forced his way over amid a crowd of bodies but his effort was ruled out after a long review for a ruck infringement.

It mattered little as the visitors scored from their next possession with Carre crashing over from close range to level the scores.

Argentina turned up the heat with two more tries to lead 28-14 at half-time.

Kremer drove over before Carreras finished off a more flowing attack after a sustained spell of pressure.

The hosts took a firm grip on proceedings after the restart as Piccardo sent the supporting No 8 Oviedo over for his second of the contest.

Wales refused to give up and gave themselves a glimmer of hope as prop Warren found space to touch down but Argentina comfortably saw out the closing stages.

Argentina will host England for their third Nations Championship fixture at Estadio Unico in Santiago del Estero on Saturday July 18 (8.10pm kick-off).

Wales will travel to South Africa for their third Test of the summer, also on Saturday July 18, at Kings Park Stadium in Durban (4.40pm kick-off).

articles.title: Nations Championship: England rugby players to avoid wearing national shirts in Argentina as football counterparts face off at World Cup
articles.summary: England second-row Alex Coles reveals the rugby squad will avoid wearing national shirts in Argentina this week ahead of Nations Championship contest against the Pumas on Saturday (8pm kick-off BST), in light of Wednesday's FIFA World Cup meeting between England and Argentina in the USA
articles.body:
Steve Borthwick's side will be in Buenos Aires when Wednesday's FIFA World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina takes place.

The squad wore England jerseys in support of the football team for last Saturday's quarter-final against Norway, but did so in Liverpool after defeating Fiji earlier in the day.

"I think, bearing in mind where we are and who we're playing with, we've been pretty sensible about not wearing our English shirts around too much," lock Alex Coles told The Telegraph.

"We had them all out in Liverpool and got a bit of a better reception than we might do here.

"I definitely love my football. I think there's a fair bunch of us that do. We watched the previous game after our game at the weekend, on in a rooftop bar in Liverpool, and it was very cool. Everyone was getting very excited.

"We're very proud to represent our country playing rugby, and I think that translates to real excitement around watching England in any sport, and World Cup fever - it is sort of like no other with the football, isn't it?

"It captures the imagination of the globe in a way that no other sport can. It's really special, and I think it's the sport that I grew up watching first before rugby and cricket, football was the thing I was obsessed with."

England wing Tommy Freeman said the squad are ready for an "angry" atmosphere and contest against the Pumas on Saturday, should England's footballers prove victorious in Atlanta.

"We'll see how hostile it gets," said Freeman.

"It's big for Argentina and us and being here it's heightened massively. I think they'll probably be angry if we win so Saturday could be a tough game.

"We know they're a passionate country. We are too and they'll want to compete to the fullest and we'll be ready for that."

articles.title: England captain Jamie George will lead team off field in Argentina if racial abuse resurfaces
articles.summary: Jamie George won't flinch taking matters into his own hands if racial abuse directed at Asher Opoku-Fordjour and Chandler Cunningham-South occurs again in Argentina; Los Pumas host England in Santiago del Estero on weekend three of rugby's inaugural Nations Championship
articles.body:
Asher Opoku-Fordjour and Chandler Cunningham-South were targeted by a small group of fans when warming up with their fellow replacements during the first half of England's 22-17 victory in San Juan a year ago.

A World Rugby investigation concluded that an act of racial discrimination had taken place and the Argentine Rugby Union has provided assurances that it was a one-off episode.

If a similar incident does unfold at the Estadio Unico Madre de Ciudades, George insists England are ready to take matters into their own hands - including by returning to the changing room.

"It's something being considered," the captain said. "If anything like that happened then it deserves the strongest of reactions. There is no place for that in the world and I feel incredibly strongly about that.

"We've had discussions around 'what if?'. I really hope - and I'm optimistic - that the Argentinian Rugby Union has taken it very seriously. At the same time we've got a plan B if that doesn't happen.

"The first thing we'd do is make the referee aware of what we've seen so it can be properly logged and all the protocols can go into play. What we do outside of that we're still deciding."

George is consulting with those members of England's squad with mixed heritage before determining what action to take, including Opoku-Fordjour, who is included on the bench for the climax to the July tour.

"It's something I will remember for the rest of my life when I heard what had happened - and it wasn't directed at me," said George, who was a late withdrawal from the starting XV in San Juan after being called up for the Lions tour to Australia but was present for the game.

"It was directed at my team-mates and I care about my team-mates more than anything.

"I will continue to have conversations with a select group of players from different ethnic backgrounds and we will come up with a plan.

"Asher's obviously aware of what's coming and he's had conversations with a few of the other guys. I'm going to him because this isn't just my call to make - the abuse wasn't aimed at me."

England have won all five of their meetings with Argentina in the Steve Borthwick era, including their most recent clash at Allianz Stadium in November when flanker Tom Curry was involved in a tunnel bust-up with Pumas coach Felipe Contepomi.

"It's a big rivalry now," George said. "We look at Argentina on the calendar whenever the fixtures come out and we know it will be a special occasion.

"On the field we're very aware that when we play Argentina they're an incredibly proud nation and it's going to be hostile.

"They're going to be desperate to win, especially on their own turf."

articles.title: Fiji 17-33 Scotland: Jamie Dobie scores twice as Scots fight back from 10 points behind to win Nations Championship clash
articles.summary: Gregor Townsend made 14 changes for Scotland's final match of the summer and was almost made to pay as Fiji led 17-7 at half-time; however four second-half tries ensured  a bonus-point win at Murrayfield
articles.body:
Fellow replacements Pierre Schoeman and Scott Cummings also grabbed tries as Scotland overturned a 10-point deficit to triumph at Murrayfield.

Gregor Townsend had made 14 changes for Scotland's final summer encounter and Jonny Gray had opened the scoring before Fiji responded with three first-half tries, the final one when they were temporarily down to 14 men.

But Townsend turned to his bench after the break and Fiji's resistance was broken as Scotland dominated the final half hour to seal the bonus-point win.

Scotland were looking to build on an impressive win in Argentina and a spirited defeat in South Africa as they hosted Fiji in what was technically an away game.

The Scots had some strong early pressure before scoring in the 14th minute. George Horne was halted on the five-metre line just before Gray managed to touch down despite the efforts of two opponents to keep the ball off the ground. Horne converted.

Fiji were ahead within five minutes though, showing their intent to attack when Gregor Brown was penalised for holding on to the ball on the ground. A kick for touch soon led to a try as Tevita Ikanivere crossed from the lineout maul.

Their second try was more typical of Fiji rugby traditions as they broke from deep in their own half before winger Selestino Ravutaumada finished brilliantly, a grubber kick taking him away from Josh Bayliss.

Ravutaumada was shown a yellow card following a head-on-head challenge on Horne but it was the underdogs who added to the scoring before the break. A cross-field kick put Scotland on the back foot and Elia Canakaivata surprised everyone at the breakdown by turning and running for the line through a huge gap before launching himself between the posts.

Fiji converted through Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula to lead 17-7 at the break.

Townsend's side were still lacking creativity in the opening stages of the second half but the substitutions immediately made an impact. Schoeman forced his way over in the 53rd minute after captain Stafford McDowall carried well following a lineout.

Scotland were quickly back on the attack. Duhan van der Merwe and Schoeman were stopped just short of the line before Bayliss got over but saw the ball pop out of his grasp.

With regular skipper Sione Tuipulotu among the experienced players to come off the bench, Scotland found more tempo to their play and Dobie squeezed between the post and a Fijian to ground the ball on the line in the 61st minute, with the try standing after lengthy examination of the footage.

Cummings produced a close-range finish in the 74th minute, with Fergus Burke completing a hat-trick of conversions.

Van der Merwe soon won an aerial ball before feeding Bayliss, who set up Dobie in the corner to round off the scoring.

'We've got players who can make a difference'

Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend on his replacements:

"They were very good. I think they obviously lifted the players as well who were on the field. They added in terms of the carrying and the effort, but I felt those guys who went 80 minutes, they dug deep.

"It shows we've got good depth and we made 14 changes this week. We've gone up against a really good Test side who played their best rugby of the campaign.

"It's a team that beat us last year, but also knowing that we've got players that can make a difference on the bench is reassuring.

"Two of the changes were injuries. Jonny Gray had failed his HIA and Darcy (Graham) got a whack in the side and couldn't continue as well. Gregor Brown also, it was more just cramp that he couldn't get over.

"But part of the reason behind the changes at certain times was because of injuries."

Image: Scotland's Jamie Dobie celebrates his try after coming off the bench

articles.title: Harlequins: Ugo Monye calls 48-0 Gloucester loss 'one of worst performances' he has seen
articles.summary: Ugo Monye calls former club Harlequins' 48-0 defeat by Gloucester "one of the worst performances I have ever seen".
articles.body:
Former Harlequins winger Ugo Monye has called the club's 48-0 defeat by Gloucester on Saturday "one of the worst performances I have ever seen".

Quins conceded eight tries in their heaviest league defeat for 26 years and are bottom of the early Gallagher Prem table.

"They got smashed in the scrum and the line-out. Their backfield coverage was poor. They got smashed at the gain line," Monye said on the Rugby Union Weekly podcast .

"They didn't score a single point in a league where they're literally handing out points for free [this season]."

Gloucester thrash sorry Quins to go top of the Prem

Monye, who came through the Quins academy and played over 230 games for the London club, said the players and staff may find it hard to analyse the performance in training.

"I'd love to know, when they go into their meeting and they try and draw a line under it, where they try and begin", he said.

"It was one of the worst performances I have ever seen in the Prem, by any team.

"Quins are the only club I ever played for. They're in my heart. It's so much easier if you can talk about them positively, but that's been quite difficult to do."

Harlequins finished in a lowly ninth in the Gallagher Prem last season, their worst finish in eight years, with Gloucester just above them.

But Monye said the result showed a contrast in how the two sides had gone about their summer recruitment, and suggested Quins had prioritised the marquee capture of Northampton full-back George Furbank over other areas.

"Gloucester said 'we'll have a World Cup winner in the second row, we'll have a world-class hooker, we'll have a world-class number seven' - that's money well spent," said the former England and British and Irish Lions wing.

"Quins said 'we'll have a world-class [number] 15. That's great, but first go and invest in your pack.

"They substituted the whole front row at half-time."

images.caption: Image caption, Harlequins' head coach Jason Gilmore called the performance in the 48-0 defeat at Gloucester "totally unacceptable"

articles.title: European Challenge Cup: Cheetahs to play European games in Swansea
articles.summary: South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys.
articles.body:
South African side Cheetahs will play their European Challenge Cup home matches this season at St Helen's in Swansea, the home of Welsh side Ospreys.

Cheetahs host Dragons on Sunday, 13 December and Perpignan on Sunday, 17 January with both games a day after Ospreys' home matches in the same competition.

Cheetahs have traditionally used Europe as a base for matches in the second-tier tournament, with games in the 2025-26 season taking place in Amsterdam.

There are links between Ospreys and Cheetahs. Y11 Sports & Media owns a majority stake in the Ospreys and maintain an investment interest in the South African team with players moving between both sides.

The Ospreys' first game at the redeveloped St Helen's is scheduled to be the United Rugby Championship (URC) Welsh derby against Dragons on Saturday, 24 October.

"The Ospreys are grateful to the WRU for its permission to play these matches at St Helen's," said Ospreys managing director Richard Lancaster.

"We're excited to welcome the Toyota Cheetahs for these two EPCR Challenge Cup fixtures. There is already a strong relationship between the two clubs and this is another really positive step in developing that further.

"It also demonstrates the opportunities that St Helen's can create. Having our own venue gives us the ability to bring additional high-quality rugby and events to Swansea."

Cheetahs director of rugby is former South Africa international Frans Steyn.

"It's great to be welcomed so warmly by our friends in rugby, the Ospreys," Steyn said.

"St Helen's has a proud history, and we're looking forward to playing there, experiencing the newly redeveloped stadium and making it our home in Europe."

articles.title: Marlie Packer: England forward to miss Canada and United States matches
articles.summary: Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.
articles.body:
Two-time World Cup winner Marlie Packer will not travel with England to North America this month for Tests against Canada and the United States.

The Harlequins back-rower will remain in the United Kingdom with her partner and Red Roses team-mate Rosie Galligan due to give birth.

England face Canada on 17 and 24 October (both 00:00 BST starts) before playing the USA in one-off match on 30 October (21:15 BST).

England are boosted by the return of Kelsey Clifford for the North American tour, with the Saracens prop returning from a hamstring injury.

The Red Roses continue a tough run of fixtures after playing three matches in September, beating Australia and New Zealand but ending their record-breaking winning streak with a draw against Canada.

England head coach John Mitchell described their home Tests with Canada and the Black Ferns as "humdingers that could have gone either way."

The Tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa are being viewed by England as the culmination of a self-titled three-Test series.

Mitchell described his expectations for the squad: "The 32 players travelling to North America have a great opportunity to elevate our connections as a squad because playing away from home requires togetherness.

"We have shown a real hunger to compete and improve, and we're excited to rip into our preparations and continue our rivalry with Canada in Toronto."

England also confirmed that Delaney Burns, Haidee Head and Sophie McQueen would not travel due to injury.

Harlequins back rower Packer is England's most capped active player with 119 caps.

articles.title: Argentina, rival de España para organizar el Mundial de 2035
articles.standfirst: Presenta una candidatura junto a Uruguay, Chile y Brasil y con estadios como el Monumental de Buenos Aires, Maracaná o el Nacional de Montevideo
articles.summary: Presenta una candidatura junto a Uruguay, Chile y Brasil y con estadios como el Monumental de Buenos Aires, Maracaná o el Nacional de Montevideo
articles.body: Argentina, Uruguay, Chile y Brasil, en conjunto, han presentado su candidatura para organizar el Mundial de Rugby de 2035. De concretarse, sería la primera vez que se dispute en la región. La información técnica se ha presentado a World Rugby cumpliendo en tiempo y forma los procesos de la candidatura para ser sede de Rugby World Cup 2035. La entidad madre del rugby mundial evaluará las propuestas y en noviembre de 2027 anunciará la sede elegida. El proceso previo incluye la presentación de documentación, visitas a las sedes propuestas y el anuncio en mayo de 2027 de las sedes preferidas. La decisión la tomará el Consejo de World Rugby. En la candidatura presentada, quedó establecido que, de ser elegida como la sede para RWC 2035, los cuatro países recibirán partidos del Mundial. Los estadios propuestos por la candidatura son todos icónicos y sedes de mundiales de fútbol. La candidatura sudamericana, que reúne a 232 millones de habitantes, va a tener que lidiar con otros interesados. Uno es Japón, que presentó formalmente su manifestación de interés bajo el lema promocional "No Side Spirit". Busca repetir la experiencia de 2019 y consolidar su posición como el epicentro del rugby en Asia. Otro es España, bajo el concepto "Spain Connects Rugby". Cuenta con un fuerte respaldo gubernamental, el apoyo de ligas locales y la postulación de grandes estadios del fútbol español, como el Santiago Bernabéu en Madrid, el Camp Nou en Barcelona y La Cartuja en Sevilla. Otros países que aún están evaluando si presentan su candidatura son Italia y Sudáfrica. Italia sería la primera vez que organizaría la Rugby World Cup y es el único del Seis Naciones que no tuvo partidos de Mundial de Rugby en su territorio. Sudáfrica la organizó en 1995, año en el que jugaron por primera vez y ganaron la primera de las 4 que tiene en sus vitrinas. ¿Qué oportunidades tiene Sudamérica? En el momento de elegir, World Rugby evalúa muchas cosas. Vamos a ver algunas que pueden jugar a favor y otras que puedan jugar en contra. A favor: - Es la primera vez que se juega un mundial en la región, lo que ayuda al desarrollo, crecimiento y llegada del deporte a todos los rincones del planeta. - Argentina, país que creció mucho en el mundo del rugby en los últimos 30 años, lidera la propuesta, con mayor cantidad de partidos en su territorio. Sería un reconocimiento al aporte argentino en estos años. - Uruguay y Chile son países emergentes en el deporte, de gran crecimiento en los últimos 8 años. El mundial les daría un espaldarazo. En contra - En 2031 el Mundial se juega en Estados Unidos. Si bien son dos confederaciones distintas, quizá los países principales no quieran dos mundiales seguidos en el mismo continente. - Si bien la mayor cantidad de partidos se disputaría en Argentina, que presenta 8 estadios, Santiago de Chile está próximo a Mendoza cruzando la Cordillera de Los Andes y Montevideo está a 200 km de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, quizá las quejas puedan venir por el viaje a Río de Janeiro dado que quien tenga que jugar en la ciudad carioca deberá hacer alrededor de 2.000 km. No suena lógico quejarse por un viaje, que además es a una de las ciudades veraniegas más hermosas de Brasil y famosas del mundo. - Si el mundial sigue contando con 24 equipos, cuatro plazas de clasificación ya van a estar ocupados por los cuatro organizadores, lo que puede generar alguna protesta porque quita opciones de clasificación a tres países. Quizá, por este aspecto, se lleve la cantidad de equipos participantes a 32, lo que generaría protestas por mayor cantidad de partidos y la posibilidad de una semana más de juego. Félix Páez Molina, presidente de la Unión Argentina de Rugby, dijo, en declaraciones recogidas por la página federativa, que la presentación de esta candidatura "representa un paso muy importante para el rugby argentino y para toda la región. Tenemos la oportunidad de mostrarle al mundo nuestra pasión por este deporte, nuestra capacidad para organizar grandes eventos y todo lo que nuestros países pueden ofrecer. Es un desafío que asumimos con la profunda convicción de que nuestra región se merece una oportunidad de esta magnitud". Marcello Calandra, presidente de Sudamérica Rugby, explicó que esta presentación demuestra "cómo está unida" la región, "trabajando juntos, persiguiendo objetivos comunes". "Estamos seguros de que hemos hecho todo lo necesario para convencer a World Rugby y a Rugby World Cup de todo lo positivo que ofrecemos para ser sede. Contamos con el apoyo de nuestros gobiernos nacionales, estatales y las comunidades de rugby de los cuatro países". articles.title: Leicester Tigers hooker Finn Theobald-Thomas forced to retire
articles.summary: Leicester Tigers announce hooker Finn Theobald-Thomas retire immediately on medical grounds.
articles.body:
Leicester Tigers hooker Finn Theobald-Thomas has been forced to retire immediately on medical grounds.

The 23-year-old joined Tigers ahead of the 2023-24 season and made 33 appearances.

The Prem club did not disclose the nature of Theobald-Thomas's injury, but said , external that they and the Rugby Players' Association will "continue to support Finn as he begins the transition into retirement".

"It's difficult to put into words what rugby has meant to me," Theobald-Thomas wrote on Instagram. , external

"This isn't how I imagined my career ending, and having something I've worked towards and loved for so much of my life taken out of my hands is incredibly difficult to accept.

"But when I look back, a kid from Bradmore lived the dream of playing for his boy hood rugby club, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude. Rugby has given me some of the best moments of my life, friendships that will last forever, and memories I'll carry with me long after I've stopped playing."

Tigers head coach Geoff Parling said: "I'm gutted with this news of Finn's retirement from rugby, both from a team point of view and for him personally to have such a promising rugby journey cut short."

"He is a loveable bloke who is exactly the type of character you'd want to be around, unselfish and fully invested in the team. We'll miss him and he knows that he'll always be part of this team."

articles.title: Scarlets on their fight for existence under WRU's plan to cut a team
articles.summary: Scarlets are ready to fight for their existence as the Welsh Rugby Union presses on with controversial plans to cut a west Wales club.
articles.body:
You pass the first reminder of Llanelli's rugby identity before you even reach the town.

In Felinfoel stands a statue of Phil Bennett, a key member of the Llanelli team which famously beat New Zealand in 1972.

A few miles further on, Welsh Sports Hall of Fame inductee Ray Gravell is immortalised outside Parc y Scarlets.

There are no footballers or cricketers competing for space here. The sporting story being told is overwhelmingly one of rugby.

Which makes the question hanging over the place particularly brutal: what happens if professional rugby disappears from Llanelli?

The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans to cut its professional men's teams from four to three. Under its preferred model, Scarlets or Ospreys will cease to exist by 2028.

WRU sticking to three-team plan - Reddin

WRU seek to sell SRC side RGC to private investors

Inside Parc y Scarlets, photographs of former teams and famous victories cover the walls.

Rugby autobiographies fill a bookshelf in the cafe, where today's lunch for the players is roast beef.

The former Wales and British and Irish Lions scrum-half is back coaching at the club where he began his career. His grandfather was once a physio here, running on with the magic sponge for Gravell.

Now Peel talks about the school run and his son playing junior rugby.

It is a theme that keeps returning during a day at Parc y Scarlets with the Scrum V Podcast.

Director of rugby Nigel Davies grew up in Trimsaran, a few miles away. Peel is from nearby Tumble. A large proportion of the current squad grew up playing rugby in the towns and villages Scarlets represent.

Even managing director Jon Daniels once played for nearby Llangennech.

He believes that connection is precisely what is at stake.

"We don't have Premier League or Championship football teams," he said.

"When they want to play sport, they still play rugby in the (school) yards in west Wales."

"I genuinely fear for west Wales if this continues the way it is," Daniels said. "For the young generations of Wales, I think there would be a real loss."

It is the emotional heart of Scarlets' argument for survival.

The problem is that Welsh rugby's current predicament cannot be solved by emotion alone.

Scarlets can make their case, but cannot guarantee their own future.

Daniels argues Welsh rugby should be asking how it can preserve four teams rather than accepting one must disappear.

"We have not seen the numbers laid down in front of us to prove that we can't sustain four," he says.

But that raises an obvious question in return: where are Scarlets' numbers?

Daniels says season-ticket revenue is ahead of last year, attendances increased by 7% last season, sponsorship is performing well and the stadium is generating money away from matchdays.

But when pressed on where the additional money needed to sustain four properly funded teams would come from, there is no clear answer.

"Can we put together a 10-year plan where, in 10 years' time, we can have four competitive, successful, viable teams?" he asks.

It is an argument for more time but not yet a funded alternative, and Scarlets do not control the timetable.

On one of the cafe walls, among black-and-white photographs and faded old jerseys, is an image that looks strikingly modern.

The colours are sharp, the picture unmistakably digital. It shows Scarlets celebrating their 2017 league title - the last time a Welsh team won the competition.

James 'Cubby' Davies played in that team. Now he helps recruit the next generation.

He says the "secret sauce" was connection.

"We built success on the pitch through a lot of the things that we did off the pitch," he said. "We just connected as a group."

Davies says that uncertainty over Welsh rugby's future meant Scarlets were late entering the recruitment market last season.

There is another meeting with the WRU on the day we visit.

Davies talks about planning ahead, then hesitates.

"We're very hopeful of our... what's the word? Our existence, obviously," he said.

A strange word to hear in the everyday surroundings of a professional sports club.

On the other side of the stadium, past a couple of burger vans with their shutters still down, around 40 players are playing football in an indoor training barn.

There is shouting, laughter and arguing over decisions.

After two opening defeats and plenty of analysis, director Davies wants people smiling again.

"It's all about bringing the energy," he says.

It is striking to watch at a club whose very existence is being debated.

Daniels calls the constant speculation around Welsh rugby the "jungle drums".

"Sometimes the potential impact on human beings is lost in all that," he said.

Players train. Coaches prepare. Contracts are considered. Lunch is served.

This is what uncertainty looks like inside a sports club.

Nine miles away, another club can make its own case.

Six Ospreys were selected for the 2013 British and Irish Lions tour - twice as many as the whole of Scotland. Only two Welshmen made the Lions squad in 2025.

Ospreys are planning for the future too, with St Helen's in Swansea being redeveloped as their new home.

Llanelli's built-up area has about 42,000 people and Swansea's around 170,000. Dublin city alone has almost 600,000. Johannesburg has millions.

On a map, consolidation can look obvious. On the ground, Scarlets and Ospreys have different histories, communities and identities.

For now, Daniels refuses to accept the choice and urges caution.

"We should do that before we just jump to 'right, we cut two teams', or now 'we cut one team'," he says.

But if the WRU presses ahead with three, Scarlets and Ospreys will eventually have to make a different argument.

Not simply why they should survive, why they should survive instead of the other.

Players drift back into the cafe. Plates of roast beef appear beneath photographs of those who came before them.

For now, Scarlets continue with the strangely ordinary business of running a professional rugby club while waiting to discover whether they will remain one.

Image caption, James Davies won silver with Team GB at the 2016 Olympic sevens in Rio
Image caption, Ospreys have won three titles

articles.title: Amy Hardcastle: Bradford Bulls Women appoint St Helens centre as new head coach
articles.summary: Bradford Bulls Women appoint Amy Hardcastle as their new head coach.
articles.body:
Bradford Bulls Women have appointed Amy Hardcastle as their new head coach.

The 37-year-old centre retired from international rugby last month as England's all-time leading try scorer with 30 from 29 caps.

Hardcastle started her playing career with the Bulls and will combine the role with the National Championship side with continuing to play for Women's Super League side St Helens.

"Bradford Bulls has always been a special club to me, so the opportunity to return in this role is something that means a huge amount personally," she told the club website. , external

"I want our women's team to represent what Bradford Bulls stands for - passion, pride, hard work, togetherness and ambition.

"There is a huge amount of work ahead, but that is what makes this opportunity so exciting."

Hardcastle takes over a side that lost 11 of their 12 league games in 2026 to finish second bottom of the division.

images.caption: Image caption, Amy Hardcastle is in her second spell playing for St Helens

articles.title: Brendan Venter: Saracens media duties 'like something from an autocratic land'
articles.summary: Saracens' Brendan Venter compares Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after reluctantly speaking at a press conference.
articles.body:
Saracens' Brendan Venter compared Prem Rugby's media obligations to "something from an autocratic land" after he made a reluctant appearance at a press conference.

The 56-year-old returned to a full-time role at the club in the summer, initially as director of rugby, but has since been given an updated job title of head of culture and technical director.

His no-show at a pre-season media event cost Saracens a £5,000 fine and he avoided questions before and after the club's opening-round win over Leicester.

However, he appeared alongside head coach Joe Shaw to preview this Saturday's match against Bristol and, after initially offering only short answers to reporters' questions, railed against the expectation that he would be the public face of the club.

"I have the desire as a human being not to want to talk," he said. "It is not about me, it is about the team… I expressed that desire before I came."

Venter added: "I asked really kindly and eventually I bent over backwards to explain my position. And then I'm expected again to come and do an interview.

"If we get obsessed, get into an argument and fine a club, that for me does not make sense.

"It sounds like something from an autocratic land, not a democracy where people have the right to say: 'This is what I want to do'.

"If you want an interview, you have a brilliant person in Joe. I do not have the desire to do an interview. It stole my joy the previous time and I want to have a low profile.

"That was my desire and to help to coach the rugby team. I do not want to be doing interviews. It's not because I think I'm better than anybody else. To be put over as an arrogant person who thinks he's better than doing interviews… it's not at all that."

Venter's previous 16-month spell in charge of Saracens was littered with controversy.

He also ignored the obligation for club captain Steve Borthwick to attend a Heineken Cup launch event, instead sending the now England coach on a beer-fuelled team-bonding trip to Munich.

After one reprimand by European rugby authorities, Venter gave a viral post-match interview, inspired by a scene from the film Mike Bassett: England Manager, , external in which he agreed with the premise of every question asked of him.

After leaving Saracens in 2011, Venter, who won the Rugby World Cup as a player with South Africa in 1995, worked in roles with Durban-based club side the Sharks, as well as with Italy and South Africa.

The changes to his job title since his return to north London, which reportedly included a stint as the club's wine consultant that lasted a matter of days, , external appeared to be an attempt to escape his media obligations.

Prem Rugby rules require the most senior coach in every club to carry out routine media duties.

Their job titles can vary. Rob Baxter is Exeter's director of rugby. George Skivington is Gloucester's head coach. But as the principle decision-maker for their team, both answer questions each week.

Venter claimed in a weekend interview with TNT Sport, the broadcaster who pays £40m a season for action and access to the Prem, that decisions over team selection are done on the basis of a consensus, rather than any single person having a final say.

Regardless, it is expected the Venter will continue to face the media for the rest of the campaign.

Venter added that, despite his reservations, he had been tempted back by a love of coaching and the high-intensity dressing room environment.

"I love coaching rugby. I love working with players. It is a privilege we get as human beings to be in a position where we can influence things, both good and bad," he added.

"People in life rarely get that privilege.

"It's a phenomenal game to be a part of and that's why when [Saracens owner] Dominic [Silvester] asked me, I agreed to come back.

"You make friends like you never make in your life. When there are good times and difficult times, it builds character. I'm privileged enough to be doing that on a daily basis."

Venter did not win any silverware during his first stint in charge of Saracens. His side lost to Leicester in the 2010 Premiership final, a match Venter was banned from as part of a touchline suspension.

However, he left behind a formidably talented and closely bonded squad who would win multiple domestic and European honours under McCall in the following decade.

In behind-the-scenes footage of Venter's speech to his squad at the start of pre-season, he set out his ambition to contend for the Prem title.

"I promise you I don't want to be competitive in this league. I want to dominate," he said.

"This is not a team with a ceiling, this is something special, I have not come all this way to be average."

images.caption: Image caption, Brendan Venter appeared alongside head coach Joe Shaw (left) to preview Saracens' game against Bristol on Saturday
Image caption, England boss Borthwick was Venter's Saracens captain during the South African's first stint in charge of the club

articles.title: Shanelle Williams: Wales hooker realises childhood dream and prepares for Japan
articles.summary: Shanelle Williams has realised a childhood dream of playing for Wales and now the hooker wants more caps, beginning with two Tests against Japan in WXV.
articles.body:
Shanelle Williams has already fulfilled one childhood ambition after making her Wales debut and now she is preparing for another milestone in Japan.

The 19-year-old former Gwernyfed RFC junior came off the bench in Wales' 50-19 win over South Africa in the WXV Global Series in September.

As a child, Williams had written on her Christmas list that she wanted to play for Wales.

"I didn't actually know that there was a women's team," the hooker said.

"I used to tell my dad that I was going to play for Wales with the boys.

"Then I obviously realised that I actually can play for Wales. Since then, everything I've done, rugby's always been a priority."

Williams had forgotten about the Christmas list until her older sister reminded her after she won her first Wales Under-18 cap.

"It's quite a nice reminder that I have been working for this for so long, so it has all been worth it," she said.

Williams started playing rugby at Gwernyfed aged eight, spending four years there before joining the Red Kites and later moving into the Wales pathway.

She went on to play for Cardiff Quins and Cardiff Rugby before attending Hartpury College.

Her father played a key role, regularly making the journey from home to Cardiff for training.

"Obviously I'm from Gwernyfed, so it was about an hour and a half down to Cardiff," she said.

"He used to take me for training on Friday nights straight after school.

"I wouldn't have been able to do it if my dad hadn't given me that opportunity, so I'm very lucky."

Williams' family and friends were in the stands to watch her make her Wales debut at Cardiff Arms Park.

"They'll come to every single game that they can," she said.

"It's so nice to be able to have that support on the sideline. I can always hear them over everyone else in the crowd."

Williams says the reality of becoming a senior Wales international only really sank in once she stepped onto the pitch.

"It didn't feel real it until I was actually on the pitch," she said.

"It was quite nice to be able to come onto the pitch with Elan (Jones) as well, because we've done [Wales] Under-18s together, we've done Under-20s together.

"Being able to share that with her was really nice as well. Then coming to my family afterwards, it was a surreal feeling, to be honest."

The Brython Thunder hooker has been inclued in a 30-player squad for two Tests against Japan which will complete Wales' WXV Global Series campaign for 2026.

The first Test takes place at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo on Saturday, 24 October at 10:30 BST, with the second at Kumagaya Rugby Stadium in Saitama seven days later at 07:00 GMT.

Williams admits the senior international environment has been a significant step up.

"I'd heard a lot from my friends - 'It is a step up, it is a step up'," she said.

"I think that actually prepared me quite well to understand that it's not just going into another pathway camp.

"There's even more competition and also understanding that there are still people behind you chasing for your position as well. I think that pushes you a lot more.

"So yeah, it's definitely been a step up, but I've been enjoying it."

Metcalfe back in Wales WXV reckoning for Japan

Lynn remaining positive despite Wales' USA setback

Lions tour a 'top goal' for Wales prop Tuipulotu

'It's the longest flight I've ever been on'

Japan will also provide Williams with a new experience off the pitch.

"It's the longest flight I've ever been on," she said.

"I've only ever been to Italy, I think that's the furthest I've been - two hours. So I'm not sure how that's going to go."

But she is determined to make the most of her opportunity against a Japan side ranked 12th in the world, one place below Wales.

"Sometimes, because they're not in the Six Nations and stuff, they can be a little bit overlooked," she said.

"They are a good team, so it's just making sure we stay on top of our process.

"We've done a lot over pre-season on being an 80-minute team, so I think sticking to that should help us."

Williams has already achieved the dream she wrote down as a child. Now she wants to add to her Wales cap tally.

"I've always looked up to girls like Kelsey Jones, Molly Reardon and Carys Phillips when she was in the squad," she said.

"They've always been role models to me, so being able to train alongside them and get tips from them as well is really beneficial to me.

"Definitely, I want to add to that tally."

images.caption: Image caption, Shanelle Williams is looking for more Wales caps after the hooker's debut off the bench against South Africa
